smart-home.title: A thermostat you can build: radar presence, a touch screen, Matter into Apple Home
smart-home.one_line: Three boards and four wires. An IWRL6432BOOST radar board sees whether anyone is in the room, an LP-MSPM0G3519 draws the thermostat screen, and an LP-EM-CC35X1 is the Matter thermostat that Apple Home controls from the phone.

pictures.alt: The Home app on an iPhone showing a Matter accessory heating to 67 with the current temperature 69
pictures.caption: In the Home app: the Matter thermostat on the LP-EM-CC35X1, setpoint moved from the phone (2026-10-11)

pictures.alt: The thermostat demo on the bench: a 3.5 inch display showing Room is empty, 20.8 C and a 21.5 C setpoint in Fox Red Labs colors, with the three boards wired around it
pictures.caption: The whole demo: the screen on the LP-MSPM0G3519, the LP-EM-CC35X1 beside it and the radar board behind (2026-10-12)

pictures.alt: Two LaunchPad boards on the bench joined by a bundle of jumper wires, one with a whip antenna
pictures.caption: The screen board and the radio board, wired: the LP-MSPM0G3519 sends one status line a second to the LP-EM-CC35X1 (2026-10-12)

pictures.alt: The IWRL6432BOOST radar board straight on, antenna patterns at the left, three LEDs lit
pictures.caption: The radar: an IWRL6432BOOST, antennas on the board, no lens, no camera (2026-10-12)

facts: Apple Home pairs and controls the thermostat (LP-EM-CC35X1, Matter over Wi-Fi)
6 to 8 screen refreshes a second with the radar live, no dropped frames (LP-MSPM0G3519)
Radar frames reach the screen in under 50 ms (replay runs)
